newsitem.title: USA: Miami to re-enter debt market with note sale.
newsitem.headline: Miami to re-enter debt market with note sale.

text.p: Miami tentatively plans to re-enter the debt market with a $25 million tax anticipation note sale in the fall, city officials said Monday.

The note sale probably will take place in "very early October or very late September," Assistant City Manager Bob Nachlinger said at a meeting of the state-appointed oversight board guiding the city's financial recovery.
He said the issue probably would be underwritten by a local bank or banks.
"We've already had interest from the local banking community that they'd be interested to bid on it," Nachlinger said.

The city has used similarly sized TANs in the past to meet cash flow needs between the start of the fiscal year on Oct 1 and the time the bulk of property tax revenues are received in December and January.

Last year's planned TAN sale was scrapped after the city revealed it had a $68 million budget deficit in its $275 million budget. The problems prompted Standard & Poor's Corp to cut Miami's general obligation bond rating to single-B, with a negative watch, and Moody's Investors Service to cut it to Ba1. Both ratings represent junk or non-investment grades.
Asked if the city's financial status had improved enough to make borrowing costs reasonable, Nachlinger said, "We'll find out."
The note issue would require approval from the oversight board appointed by Gov. Lawton Chiles to help Miami mend its budget problems.
Lt. Gov. Buddy MacKay, who chairs the board, said "There's not a lot of risk in it" because the borrowing would be so short term.
